primitives.name: Data Integrity Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Integrity rule Do not pretend blocked, metadata-only, fixture-backed, license-required, or partner-required data is active.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I': 'Boolean indicator for data integrity (dimensionless)', 'B': 'Blocked data flag (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: All data must be either active or explicitly marked as blocked; no implicit activation of restricted data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When I = 0, B = 1, indicating non-conformant data access.

layer2.mapping: Integrity gate maps to GSI's Bayesian data validation layer, where blocked data is excluded from probabilistic inference.
layer2.telemetry: Active data count vs blocked data count ratio

primitives.name: Source Activation Queue
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Human action minimized Every blocked source is isolated into rights/activation/outreach queues with fallback source, expected next action, and product impact.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q': 'Queue state vector (dimensionless)', 'F': 'Fallback source identifier (categorical)', 'A': 'Expected next action (categorical)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each blocked source has a deterministic fallback path and defined action sequence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Q = ∅, system enters failure mode due to no viable activation path.

layer2.mapping: Activation queue is derived from GSE's state transition engine, where blocked data triggers fallback logic.
layer2.telemetry: Queue depth and fallback resolution time

The core duality in StatKing’s architecture lies between data integrity and activation efficiency. The integrity gate ensures that only validated data enters the system, while the activation queue manages the flow of blocked data through fallback mechanisms. Product readiness scores act as a scalar filter that determines whether new data can be integrated. These operators form a closed-loop system where each primitive influences the others: integrity gates prevent invalid inputs, activation queues ensure continuity, and readiness scores enforce quality thresholds. Failure modes occur when integrity checks fail, queues overflow, or readiness drops below critical levels. The system's robustness depends on maintaining this balance through dynamic feedback loops.
